newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Siemens mulls further Portugal investments.
newsitem.headline: Siemens mulls further Portugal investments.

text.p: German group Siemens AG is considering building another electronics factory as well as investing in some other projects in Portugal, its managing director in Portugal was quoted as saying on Tuesday.

Carlos de Melo Ribeiro told the Exame monthly that Siemens had already submitted a dossier to the government envisaging the possible construction of an electronic components factory in Evora in the depressed Alentejo region of southern Portugal.

A decision to proceed with the eight billion escudo ($52 million) investment would depend on any incentives that the Socialist government would be prepared to offer in competition against other countries, the Exame said in its October edition.
A Siemens spokesman confirmed the information when contacted by Reuters. He said no timetable had been set for decisions.
Siemens is currently building a memory chips factory in northern Portugal, the second biggest foreign investment in the country.
Newspapers have said the government is providing financial incentives accounting for 49 percent of the investment expected to total 78 billion escudos by the year 2000.
The factory in northern Portugal is expected to be built by the end of 1997 and to produce up to 150 million chips per year for the world market. It should create 750 jobs by the year 2000.
